# Roadbeat

> Roadbeat is a free web app for live Queensland road conditions and public transport: QLDTraffic road events and cameras, Translink vehicles, departures and published timetables, a timetable-based journey planner, Queensland Fire Department bushfire warnings, Queensland's storm, flood and cyclone warnings, satellite hotspots and imagery, Brisbane City Council and Queensland Government stream gauges, air quality, Energex power outages and council notices, traffic signal volumes and planned road closures, Queensland Rail station access details with Translink's lift and escalator outages, and a map of police, council and news reports. It shows only data that official sources publish and never estimates times, positions or delays.

## When to use Roadbeat

- Someone asks what is happening on a Queensland road right now: crashes, closures, roadworks, flooding or congestion.
- Someone wants the next departures from a Translink stop or station, or a line's full timetable for a given day.
- Someone wants a direct public transport trip, or a trip with one change at the same station or stop, from Queensland's published timetable.
- Someone asks about current bushfire warnings in Queensland, Brisbane creek and river heights and rainfall, or the latest height at a Queensland river gauging station.
- Someone needs to know whether a train station or ferry terminal has a working lift, level boarding, accessible toilets or parking, or how easy a Brisbane bus stop is to board.
- Someone wants to know if a Brisbane clearway is in effect, or where the nearest accessible public toilet or accessible parking bay is.
- Someone wants to see what Brisbane City Council events are on this week near a place, with the council's own details.
- Someone wants a shareable link to a specific road event, stop, line, fire warning or journey search.

## When not to use Roadbeat

- Emergencies: call Triple Zero (000).
- Trips that need walking between stops, more than one change, or fares: use Translink's journey planner at https://jp.translink.com.au/plan-your-journey/journey-planner.
- Flood warnings: Roadbeat shows raw gauge heights without flood levels, and links each gauge to the Bureau of Meteorology's warning for its area. Use BoM for warnings.
- Places outside Queensland.

## Pages

- [Home](%SITE_URL%/): the live map and lists.
- [About](%SITE_URL%/about/): what Roadbeat is, its data sources and its accuracy rule.
- [Glossary](%SITE_URL%/glossary/): what warning levels, road closures and restrictions mean, quoted from the agencies that publish them, and which terms have no official definition.
<!--if:GA_MEASUREMENT_ID-->
- [Privacy](%SITE_URL%/privacy/): no accounts or advertising; Google Analytics counts visits; settings stay in the browser.
<!--endif-->
<!--ifnot:GA_MEASUREMENT_ID-->
- [Privacy](%SITE_URL%/privacy/): no accounts, ads or cookies; visits are counted without identifying you; settings stay in your browser.
<!--endif-->
- [Contact](%SITE_URL%/contact/): how to reach Roadbeat and where to report problems with official data.
- [Stations](%SITE_URL%/stations/): a page per train station, tram stop and ferry terminal in South East Queensland (`%SITE_URL%/stations/central-station/`), with its lines, platforms, published position and nearby localities.
- [Lines and routes](%SITE_URL%/lines/): a page per Translink line and regional route (`%SITE_URL%/lines/t1-caboolture/`, `%SITE_URL%/lines/tsv-200/`), with the stops it serves.
- [Places](%SITE_URL%/places/): a page per Queensland town, suburb or locality (`%SITE_URL%/places/goodna/`), with its council area, gazetteer position and nearby stations.

The directory pages hold published facts only; each ends with the app link for live departures or what is happening there now.

Every page is also available as Markdown: send `Accept: text/markdown`, or add `.md` to the page path (for example `%SITE_URL%/about.md`).

## API and MCP server

Roadbeat answers live questions for AI agents and apps. Both are free, read-only and need no key. Every answer names its official source.

- MCP server (Streamable HTTP): `%SITE_URL%/mcp`. Tools: `road_events` (search Queensland road events by road and place), `find_stops` (Translink stops by name), `next_departures` (real-time departures from a stop, optionally one route) and `bushfire_warnings`. Discovery card: `%SITE_URL%/.well-known/mcp.json`.
- REST API: `%SITE_URL%/api/events?q=Bruce%20Highway%20Gympie`, `%SITE_URL%/api/stops?q=Central`, `%SITE_URL%/api/departures?stop=place_censta&route=T6`, `%SITE_URL%/api/bushfires`. OpenAPI description: `%SITE_URL%/openapi.json`.

Departure times come from Translink's real-time feed, which covers services running now or starting soon. A delay is reported as tracked only when a vehicle on that trip is reporting its position.

## Linking to views in the app

The app keeps its current view in the URL hash, so these links open a view directly:

- `%SITE_URL%/#event/<id>`: a QLDTraffic road event.
- `%SITE_URL%/#camera/webcam-<id>` or `#camera/floodcam-<id>`: a traffic or flood camera.
- `%SITE_URL%/#transit/line/<mode>/<name>`, for example `#transit/line/train/T1%20Caboolture`: a line's status, departures and timetable.
- `%SITE_URL%/#transit/stop/<region>/<stop id>`, for example `#transit/stop/SEQ/place_censta` or `#transit/stop/TSV/890194`: a stop's departures and full-day timetable.
- `%SITE_URL%/#transit/route/<region>/<route code>`, for example `#transit/route/TSV/V200`: a route outside South East Queensland, with its alerts, departures where Translink publishes real-time for the region, and its timetable.
- `%SITE_URL%/#transit/trip/SEQ/<trip id>/<route>[/<YYYY-MM-DD>]`: one trip's stops in order with published times and Translink's real-time times where reported.
- `%SITE_URL%/#transit/plan/SEQ/<from stop id>/<to stop id>[/<YYYY-MM-DD>/<minutes after midnight>/<leave|arrive>]`: a journey search.
- `%SITE_URL%/#fire/<warning id>`: a Queensland Fire Department warning or incident.
- `%SITE_URL%/#gauge/<sensor id>`: a Brisbane City Council stream or rain gauge (e.g. E1594), or a Queensland Government stream gauging station (e.g. 143001C).
- `%SITE_URL%/#signal/<SCATS number>`: a Brisbane City Council signalised intersection.
- `%SITE_URL%/#place/clearway/<id>`, `#place/toilet/<id>`, `#place/bay/<id>`, `#place/meter/<meter number>`, `#place/bike/<id>`, `#place/clearance/<id>` or `#place/event/<Trumba event id>`: a Brisbane clearway, public toilet, accessible parking bay, parking meter, bike rack, low clearance or council event.

## Data sources

All are published under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 unless noted.

- Department of Transport and Main Roads: road events, cameras, rest areas, truck restrictions and crash history (QLDTraffic feeds and data.qld.gov.au). Rain radar images are the Bureau of Meteorology's, as QLDTraffic publishes them.
- Translink: GTFS timetables and GTFS-RT vehicle positions, trip updates and service alerts for South East Queensland and Cairns, and published timetables for the 17 other regional networks (real-time too where Translink's feed for that region carries data).
- Queensland Fire Department: current bushfire incidents and warnings.
- Queensland Disaster Management (disaster.qld.gov.au): severe weather, flood and cyclone warnings, as published (CC BY 4.0).
- Brisbane City Council: bus stop audits, clearways, parking meters, bikeways and bike racks, public toilets (National Public Toilet Map), accessible parking, council events, ferry terminals, the February 2022 flood extent, telemetry gauges, intersection volumes, planned temporary road occupancies, CBD car park spaces, and Queensland Rail's railway station facilities (data.brisbane.qld.gov.au).
- Department of Local Government, Water and Volunteers: the latest stream heights at open gauging stations (Water Monitoring Information Portal, water-monitoring.information.qld.gov.au) and the station list (data.qld.gov.au).
- Bureau of Meteorology: National Flood Gauge Network catchments (data.gov.au).
- Department of Environment, Tourism, Science and Innovation: hourly air quality and each station's history (Air Quality API).
- Geoscience Australia: Digital Earth Australia satellite hotspots and recent earthquakes.
- NASA Global Imagery Browse Services: the daily NOAA-20 satellite image (no use restrictions), the daily Terra morning image, and the Japan Meteorological Agency's Himawari-9 image every 10 minutes (JMA Public Data License).
- Japan Meteorological Agency: Himawari-9 infrared and true-colour images from its weather map (Source: Japan Meteorological Agency website).
- Queensland Police Service: media releases.
- 58 Queensland councils' disaster dashboards: bulletins, evacuation centres, council cameras and notices, and the Energex power outages they relay (no licence published; shown as written, linked to each dashboard).
- News outlets (ABC News, 7NEWS, Brisbane Times, Guardian Australia, SBS News): headline, link and first sentence only, under each publisher's terms.
- OpenFreeMap, OpenMapTiles and OpenStreetMap contributors: base maps (ODbL).

Roadbeat is independent and is not affiliated with, or endorsed by, the Queensland Government.
